selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does sunset make a person remember about the beautiful living things of summer and autumn?
questions.answer: It reminds a person that those lovely things fade away and disappear when winter begins.

questions.question: What human event is brought to mind by Maghrib time?
questions.answer: It brings to mind a person’s death, leaving loved ones behind, and entering the grave.

questions.question: What bigger event about the whole world is also remembered at this time?
questions.answer: It reminds people that this world will also come to an end, its people will move on, and this world’s test period will close.

questions.question: Why is Maghrib a strong warning for some people?
questions.answer: It warns those who attach their hearts to temporary things and temporary beloveds.

questions.question: Why might the departures in the passage be described as sad?
questions.answer: They involve separation from things and people that are loved.

questions.question: What lesson about love and attachment is suggested here?
questions.answer: A person should not give ultimate love to things that will pass away.

questions.question: Who is especially being warned by this time of day?
questions.answer: People who devote themselves to things that do not last.

questions.question: Which prayer time is the passage focusing on?
questions.answer: It is focusing on Maghrib, the prayer at sunset.

questions.question: What season begins in the first image of the passage?
questions.answer: Winter begins.

questions.question: What happens to the gentle and attractive creatures mentioned at that point?
questions.answer: They pass away from sight and leave as the season changes.

questions.question: How is human death connected to the idea of sunset in the passage?
questions.answer: Sunset is linked with the thought that a person will one day depart from loved ones and go to the grave.

questions.question: What does the passage say will happen to the inhabitants of the world when the world dies?
questions.answer: They will be transferred from this world to other worlds.

questions.question: What does the image of a lamp being put out suggest about this world?
questions.answer: It suggests that this world’s period of testing will end.

questions.question: What kind of people are criticized in the passage?
questions.answer: People who treat passing things as if they were worthy of lasting devotion.

questions.question: What natural daily event begins the reflections in this passage?
questions.answer: The setting of the sun begins them.

questions.question: What happens to the beauties of warm seasons when the cold season starts?
questions.answer: They vanish and leave behind a sense of farewell.

questions.question: What personal future does the passage tell each person to remember?
questions.answer: Each person should remember that he or she will die, leave loved ones, and enter the grave.

questions.question: How does the passage connect personal death with the death of the world?
questions.answer: It shows both as departures from one stage to another, proving that nothing in this world remains forever.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the people living in the world at its end?
questions.answer: It says they will move on to other realms.

questions.question: What is meant by calling this world a place of examination?
questions.answer: It means this life is a temporary test, not a permanent home.

questions.question: What truth about life and death is emphasized through Maghrib time?
questions.answer: Life in this world ends, and death is a real transition that every person should remember.

questions.question: What first example of change and loss appears in the passage?
questions.answer: The first example is the disappearance of the beautiful beings of summer and autumn when winter begins.

questions.question: What second example shifts the passage from nature to human life?
questions.answer: The second example is a person’s death and separation from loved ones.

questions.question: What third example expands the message to the largest scale?
questions.answer: The third example is the death of the world and the movement of its inhabitants to other worlds.
